title: Preserve the Hard, Regenerate the Rest: Uncertainty-Guided Synthetic Training Data Augmentation with Diffusion Models
what_it_is: Ranks the GT classes of each training image by the baseline's mean entropy, keeps the most uncertain classes (about 10% of the image) pixel-exact, inpaints the rest with an off-the-shelf diffusion inpainter, and trains only on the kept pixels (inpainted pixels = ignore). Full text read: +2.07 mIoU on Cityscapes 10% (5 seeds), rare classes +9 to +12 IoU; inpainting is needed (keeping the hard pixels without new context gave only +0.53).
why_it_could_help_us: Our hard pixels are cracks and inactive; this puts the real, correctly labelled crack/inactive pixels into new backgrounds (other sources, multi half-cut pool cells) without ever supervising generated pixels, so no label noise and no seam-as-crack decoys (the CP100 failure). Targets recall on unseen modules and half-cut layout.
cost_to_try: new pipeline (offline inpainting pass + fine-tune with ignore mask)
risk_or_reason_against: Needs an EL-capable inpainter (SDXL/FLUX are RGB natural-image models; LaMa as in GDI, or a PV-DDPM retrained on train cells P042); crack class covers 0.19% of pixels so the preserve mask must be crack plus a dilated band, not the class mask alone; gains shown on natural scenes only.

title: SynthSeg: Segmentation of brain MRI scans of any contrast and resolution without retraining
what_it_is: Trains on images synthesised from label maps with fully randomised per-label intensities (GMM), bias field, gamma, and simulated low resolution (blur + downsample + upsample) while always predicting the high-resolution labels. Full text read: narrowing the intensity priors to realistic ranges lowered Dice by 1.4 to 2.6; removing bias field -3.7, removing deformation -4.3.
why_it_could_help_us: Our five sources differ mainly in contrast and blur, and E1 is a contrast/source shift. A label-conditioned intensity and resolution randomisation (crack contrast drawn independently of background, down to near-invisible; random blur/down-up per sample) attacks recall on unseen modules. Differs from GIN-IPA (P012) and SLAug (P057): intensities are sampled per label region and resolution is simulated.
cost_to_try: config-only to new pipeline (augmentation on real cells: per-label-region intensity remap + bias + blur/down-up)
risk_or_reason_against: EL background is texture (grains, fingers, busbars), not piecewise constant; pure GMM images from labels would drop it, so only the hybrid (randomise per region on real images) is plausible; brain MRI result, not thin 1 to 2 px structures (paper notes a slight drop for thin structures at low resolution).
code_available: unknown (not stated in the text read)

title: Evaluating Synthetic Data Generation for Domain Generalization in Fetal Brain MRI Segmentation (FetalSynthSeg)
what_it_is: Compares domain-randomisation generators for single-source DG: simple Gaussian-mixture intensity models beat physics-based simulation, and splitting tissue classes into intensity clusters before randomising improves out-of-domain robustness (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Tells us how to build the SynthSeg-style arm for EL: cluster the background (busbar, finger, bright/dark grain, edge) into sub-classes and randomise each, rather than writing a physics EL simulator (none exists, D06). Targets unseen-module recall.
risk_or_reason_against: MRI tissue, not thin lines; abstract only.

title: vesselFM: A Foundation Model for Universal 3D Blood Vessel Segmentation
what_it_is: Vessel segmenter trained on real data plus domain-randomised data plus mask-conditioned flow-matching samples. Full text read: zero-shot on an unseen MRA set, real only 65.45 Dice / 63.53 clDice; +DR 69.38 / 72.10; +flow 74.66 / 75.27. Conditioning the generator on synthetic masks instead of real masks was better by 4.54 Dice (real masks carry annotator errors). Synthetic-only training was poor (DR 55.34, flow 14.33).
why_it_could_help_us: Closest evidence that synthetic thin-structure data raises zero-shot recall/connectivity (clDice +11.7) on unseen domains; and that generator-drawn exact masks beat human masks, which matches our label-width and jitter problem. Supports a DR + mask-conditioned generator arm aimed at E1-type shifts.
cost_to_try: new pipeline (DR generator; optional flow-matching renderer)
risk_or_reason_against: 3D vessels, large real corpus (115k patches from 23 datasets); synthetic data only helped as a complement; flow-matching renderer cost as in CrackSegFlow (P024).

title: Label-Free Liver Tumor Segmentation
what_it_is: Hand-built tumour synthesis (shape from deformed ellipsoids, elastic deformation, edge blurring, texture) pasted into healthy CT. Full text read: U-Net trained on synthetic tumours only reached DSC 59.77 vs 57.51 with real labels on LiTS, higher specificity on external healthy scans, and better detection of small tumours; ablation shows that without synthetic small tumours small-tumour detection collapses.
why_it_could_help_us: External proof that a rule renderer can match real labels when the rules capture shape and boundary blur. Maps to the inactive rule renderer (region cut off from busbars by a crack, darkened by source-measured ratio; D06 row 7) for rare inactive (42 train cells), and to synthesising many faint, short cracks for low-contrast recall.
cost_to_try: new pipeline (rule renderer, no generator training)
risk_or_reason_against: Tumours are blobs; 1 to 2 px cracks are far less forgiving of renderer artefacts; CT texture is simpler than EL multi-crystalline texture.

title: Towards Generalizable Tumor Synthesis (DiffTumor)
what_it_is: Diffusion model trained on few tumour examples from one organ generates realistic small tumours in other organs; segmenters trained on these generalise across patient groups, protocols and hospitals (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Same structure as our E1 problem: few labelled defects from some sources, deploy on unseen modules. Suggests training a defect generator on all five sources and rendering small/faint defects onto pool cells of the target type (incl. multi half-cut) for recall on unseen modules.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; latent-diffusion blur on 1 to 2 px cracks (D06 point 4); compute.

title: DiffCrack: A semantic-structural controllable framework for crack image generation in complex scenes
what_it_is: Mask-conditioned crack diffusion with prompt attributes (width, depth, colour, texture) and width normalisation of masks. Full text read: replacing real CrackTree260 images by synthetic ones raised precision but cut recall and F1; fine-tuning on 1,000 synthetic images raised F1 on EdmCrack600 complex scenes by 17 to 28 points (3 seeds, 3 backbones).
why_it_could_help_us: Two lessons for us: synthetic cracks act as a precision regulariser and can lower recall (recall on unseen modules is our weak point), so any synthetic crack arm must be judged on relR@2; and controlling width/contrast per sample is how to cover faint cracks.
risk_or_reason_against: Pavement cracks normalised to 20 to 23 px; paper states that narrow masks give too-subtle cracks, so 1 to 2 px EL cracks are outside its working range; latent diffusion.

title: MaskFactory: Towards High-quality Synthetic Data Generation for Dichotomous Image Segmentation
what_it_is: Edits real masks (rigid viewpoint and non-rigid topology-consistent edits) then renders high-resolution image-mask pairs with multi-condition control; for fine-structure (DIS5K) segmentation (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Mask-editing step is the part that transfers: topology-consistent deformation of real crack masks to make new crack geometries, and of cell layouts toward half-cut geometry, before rendering.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; RGB objects; renderer is latent diffusion.

title: Adapting Vision Foundation Models with Synthetic Data for Open-Pit Mining Crack Segmentation
what_it_is: Adapts SAM 3 with LoRA + LayerNorm tuning + adapters using a synthetic-only crack dataset; +18.25 pp IoU on the mining set and 69.39 mean IoU over five datasets, 10.77 pp above SegFormer trained on the same synthetic data (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Evidence that synthetic-only crack data can adapt a frozen foundation model without hurting its representation; relevant if a VFM track (other scouts) is combined with procedural EL cracks.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; mining cracks are wide; depends on SAM 3.

title: Rethinking hard training sample generation for medical image segmentation
what_it_is: Generates hard synthetic samples by pushing key-area features away from real prototypes while keeping the background faithful; polyp mIoU 86.84 over five test sets, +6.14 over CTNet (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Model-agnostic hard-sample generation; could target hard faint cracks. Lower priority than Preserve-the-Hard, which needs no generator training.

title: Generalization by Adaptation: Diffusion-Based Domain Extension for Domain-Generalized Semantic Segmentation (DIDEX)
what_it_is: Generates a diverse pseudo-target domain with a text-prompted diffusion model, then adapts the segmenter to it; +3.8 / +11.8 mIoU DG from GTA5 / SYNTHIA (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Pseudo-target-domain idea for unseen EL modules (generate source-style variants of pool cells, then self-train toward them).
risk_or_reason_against: RGB text prompts have no EL meaning; overlaps with UDA/DG family (D30).

title: Synergistic integration of text-to-image generation and deep learning for photovoltaic system inspection
what_it_is: Stable Diffusion v2 fine-tuned on 623 module-level EL images with text prompts; real+synthetic training raised YOLO precision/recall/mAP by 2 to 6 / 2 to 3 / 2 to 3.5 points. Full text read: crack and low-cell classes stayed weak (low recall); generator weights released.
why_it_could_help_us: Only open EL image generator found besides PV-DDPM; could supply extra module-level EL backgrounds/defects. Shows that synthetic EL helps boxes a little and does not fix thin-crack recall.
risk_or_reason_against: Module-level, 512 px latent diffusion, boxes only; finger interruptions and contamination could not be generated; licence of HF weights not read.

title: Towards contrast-agnostic soft segmentation of the spinal cord
what_it_is: Builds a soft ground truth by averaging the binary masks of the same subject over 6 contrasts, trains a U-Net with aggressive augmentation and a regression loss; lower cross-contrast variability (p<0.05) and better generalisation to unseen sites, vendors, contrasts (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Our label width depends on the source (1.5 to 3.25 px), so the model learns source-specific widths. A soft target that is the average of each crack skeleton rendered at every source's width convention gives one shared profile across sources, plus a regression loss; aims at thin-line precision and width-guard stability and cross-source transfer.
cost_to_try: new head or loss (soft targets + regression loss)
risk_or_reason_against: We do not have multiple annotations per cell, so the averaging is over synthetic width renderings, not real raters; crack width guard (0.85 to 1.15) must be re-checked; abstract only.
code_available: yes (in Spinal Cord Toolbox v6.2 per abstract)

title: Soft-Labelling for Budget-Constrained Semantic Segmentation: Bringing Coherence to Label Down-Sampling
what_it_is: Down-samples labels as soft class proportions instead of nearest-neighbour, so labels stay aligned with the down-sampled image; better than other label down-sampling strategies and keeps under-represented classes (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Any scale augmentation, multi-scale training or low-resolution stage deletes 1 to 2 px cracks under nearest-neighbour label resampling; soft label down-sampling keeps them. Enables resolution randomisation (SynthSeg arm) and multi-scale training without losing crack supervision.
cost_to_try: config-only (label resampling) / loss accepts soft targets
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; natural-scene datasets; we do not currently down-sample in training (fixed 512 px crops), so the value is conditional on a scale-augmentation arm.
